{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (for Customer, "Sparkling")  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement — findings, redlines and walk-away items

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The overall shape is workable for us: the licence is perpetual while fees are paid (§ 17(a)), we hold an unconditional 90-day termination right (§ 17(b)) with no early-termination fee, Garman has no convenience termination right, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitment, liquidated damages or vendor audit right burdening us. The express warranty in § 12 runs for the acceptance period plus one year and continues while Maintenance Services remain in place, with a repair remedy and no implied-warranty disclaimer — above our preferred position.

Seven items require action. Two are critical: § 13 vests ownership of the whole Work (including the bespoke Schedule "D" Modifications we pay for) in Garman and is silent on our data, and § 15 contains no monetary liability cap at all, leaving our own direct-damages exposure open-ended. Two further items sit in walk-away territory under the playbook: the blanket assignment bar (§ 20(d), reinforced by § 3(c)) with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out, and the mutual **no-hire** in § 19 covering all employees of the other party. The governing law and venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects Nova Scotia/Canada, outside our accepted list. Two clauses are missing entirely: post-termination transition assistance and return of our data, and any vendor insurance covenant — notable given that Garman attends our Authorized Locations and converts our data under § 4(b).

Three findings are recorded as **needs_review** because the automated verification check failed; in each case the rationale identifies the check as a keyword false negative and concludes the clause is acceptable (Vendor IP indemnity at the fallback and uncapped by § 15; our § 17(b) at-will exit; and the complete absence of any Garman audit right, which is better than preferred). We recommend a human confirmation pass on those three rather than any redline.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Whole Work, including Schedule "D" Modifications, owned by Garman; no title to us and no statement that we retain rights in our data. **Redline:** add data/pre-existing IP carve-out and confirm the § 2 licence covers Improvements and Modifications. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | Mutual exclusion of indirect damages and § 13/§ 14 carve-outs, but **no monetary cap** — direct damages open-ended for both parties, including for us. **Redline:** mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims; our fee obligations not treated as capped damages. |
| 3 | Critical | INDEMN — Vendor indemnification | Needs review (verification failed) | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Genuine Vendor-side IP indemnity, uncapped via the § 15 carve-out — satisfied at the fallback, no redline. Sub-elements noted only: no express duty to defend, no refund remedy, 10-day notice. **Confirm manually.** |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); § 3(c)) | Blanket consent bar both ways, no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us, no reasonableness standard — **walk-away territory** on a customer M&A event. **Redline:** affiliate/successor carve-out, reasonableness standard and no-competitor limit on Garman assignments, and confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Mutual **no-hire** reaching all employees of the other party and affiliates, no advertising/unsolicited carve-outs — **walk-away** items under the rule. **Redline:** convert to a 12-month solicitation-only restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with carve-outs. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review (verification failed) | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17(b) gives us an unconditional exit on 90 days' notice, no fee or penalty; Garman has no convenience right. Compliant at the fallback; 90-day (not 30-day) notice and silence on pro-rata refund noted only. **Confirm manually.** |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us; "exclusive" appears only in non-exclusive grants, exclusive-remedy and jurisdiction wording. No action. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee or early-termination charge; § 17(b) exit is fee-free. No action. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | § 3 limits are conventional licence-scope protections; no field-of-use or non-compete restraint on us. No action. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia/Canada law and Nova Scotia courts — vendor's home jurisdiction, outside the accepted list; venue is non-exclusive, so short of walk-away. **Redline:** New York law, exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County; Delaware, California or England and Wales offered as fallbacks. |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Licence is perpetual and covers affiliates (above walk-away), but is "non-transferable" with no successor carve-out (§§ 3(c), 20(d)) and does not cover contractors. **Redline:** extend to contractors acting on our behalf and permit transfer to an M&A successor, overriding §§ 3(c) and 20(d). |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT-adjacent / TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17 runs one way only (we return Garman materials); nothing obliges Garman to return our data or provide exit assistance, and § 18 survival omits it. **Redline:** new § 17(d) — up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No Garman audit, inspection or verification right anywhere; the only examination right (§ 16 escrow) runs in our favour. Better than preferred — inserting audit parameters would create vendor entitlement. **Confirm manually; no redline.** |
| 14 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No most-favoured-nation or best-terms mechanic in either direction. No action (we would welcome an MFN in our favour commercially). |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay or shortfall obligation; fees are for the licence and services actually taken; maintenance is a renewable one-year term. No action. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support | Renewable one-year maintenance term with no auto-renewal or non-renewal notice window — preferred position. Absence of a maintenance uplift cap noted as a sub-element only. No action. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Conformance warranty for acceptance period plus one year, continuing while under Maintenance; repair remedy and acceptance-period refund; no implied-warranty disclaimer. Exceeds preferred. No action. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 20 General Matters | No insurance covenant anywhere, yet Garman installs on our AS400s at each Authorized Location and converts our data (§§ 4, 9). **Redline:** new § 20(j) — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Assignment / change of control (§ 20(d), reinforced by § 3(c) and the "non-transferable" licence in § 2).** A blanket consent bar with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard is a walk-away on a customer M&A event. We need the affiliate/successor carve-out and confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right (§ 17 currently contains no change-of-control trigger, which we want preserved).
2. **Employee no-hire (§ 19).** A no-hire covenant, and a restriction reaching all of the counterparty's personnel rather than those involved in the services, are each walk-away items. We have narrowed to the fallback rather than deleting, given the clause is mutual.
3. **Uninsured vendor access to our sites and our data (§ 20, insurance absent).** The rationale records that a vendor which both attends our premises and processes our data without insurance is the playbook's walk-away scenario. Rated low severity on its own, but it should not survive signature unrepaired.

We also flag the two critical deviations — Garman ownership of the Modifications we commission (§ 13) and the complete absence of a liability cap (§ 15) — as items we do not expect to concede, even though they are not classified as walk-aways.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven action items: §§ 13 (IP carve-out), 15 (mutual cap with Excluded Claims), 2 (contractors and successor transfer), 20(d)/3(c) (assignment), 19 (non-solicit narrowing), 20(h) (New York law and venue), new 17(d) (transition and data return) and new 20(j) (insurance), each with a `[Playbook]` comment stating the position and the fallback.
2. **Confirm the three needs_review findings** (INDEMN, T4C, AUDIT) by human read-through; on the recorded rationales each is acceptable or better than preferred and no redline should issue.
3. **Obtain the Fee Schedule** referenced in §§ 2, 10, 11 and 17(a). It sets the cap basis under our proposed § 15 and will show whether Garman can raise maintenance fees unilaterally on renewal — if so, we pursue the CPI/3% uplift cap commercially rather than by redline.
4. **Confirm the § 4(b) data-conversion and maintenance data flows** with the business so the § 17(d) return/deletion mechanic and the cyber limit in § 20(j) are correctly scoped.
5. **Sequence the negotiation** with the three walk-away items and the two critical deviations presented as conditions of signature, and the governing-law and licence-scope points as tradeables (Delaware, California or England and Wales acceptable on law)."}
